chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from Mu'alla ibn 'Uthman from Mu'alla ibn Khunays said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not eat while leaning since Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent him, and he disliked that he resemble the kings, and we (the general public) are not able to do that.'

key_terms.مُتَّكِئٌ: Leaning (while eating, typically on the right side)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) avoid eating while leaning?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) avoided eating while leaning to distinguish himself from the ostentatious customs of kings, a practice known as *tashabbuh*. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly view that prophetic etiquette was often contextually driven by social status, implying that the general community is not bound to replicate every specific behavioral nuance of the Prophet if the underlying reason (royal distinction) does not apply to them.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Moala Bin Usman, from Moala Bin Khunays who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not eat whilst leaning since Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent him<sup>saww</sup>, and he<sup>saww</sup> disliked that he<sup>saww</sup> resembles with the kings, and we (the public) are not able that we do it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan from Mu‘alla’ ibn ‘Uthman from Mu‘alla’ ibn Khunayth who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Holy Prophet never ate while leaning against something, from the time Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent him as His Messenger. He (the Messenger of Allah) disliked sitting as kings, but we are not able to do so.’”
